acceptance_scope: Narrow Stage0 prototype per specification section 41; does not accept linked production/MVP features
assertion: В тестовом Backend RCE попытаться подделать plan/approval, перезаписать DB, вызвать Broker IPC, запросить secret и Docker operation; ожидать отказ для shell/несоответствующего scope/невалидного IPC. Если тест демонстрирует злоупотребление разрешённым выглядит approval в пределах TCB, это **показывается как остаточный риск, не маскируется фразой «RCE защищён»**; разработчик подтверждает заявленную границу доверия.
environment: Disposable GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04.5; Python 3.13 unit/native labs, Python 3.12 QEMU harness; Docker 29.9.3, Compose 2.38.2, age 1.3.2; no user VPS/SSH keys
fault_injection: Forge approval, call Broker, request shell, raw secret, arbitrary Docker and outside-scope operations
initial_state: Backend container able to rewrite application approval/plan records
limits: Automated self-review, not an independent human security audit.
QEMU guests, managed services and SFTP share one hypervisor; external operator/offline Owner roles are automated fixture processes.
Independent VPS/targets in dependency tests are inventory scopes on the fixture runner, not independently administered production machines.
SIGKILL/ENOSPC phase-boundary injection does not prove physical power-loss or arbitrary filesystem/storage durability.
Backend approval authority and managed root/Docker daemon remain within the stated TCB; knowingly false Owner attestation is not detected with a guarantee.
Lab dependency SBOM is scoped and incomplete for a production release; package install/update/restore integration remains unaccepted.
observation: Compromised Backend rewrites SQLite approvals but has no direct Broker mount, Vault read or Docker socket. Worker forwarding arbitrary shell, raw decrypt/Docker requests, foreign scopes and forged permits is denied. Apparently approved in-scope forgery receives a scoped receipt: explicit Backend-in-TCB residual risk, not RCE protection. The receipt is a lab admission result, not execution of an arbitrary remote Docker operation; replay is denied.
